visible.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy uses DEA Form 106 as though it were the ordering document for an ordinary Schedule II stock purchase.

Case B: The pharmacy returns eligible Schedule II stock to an authorized supplier and assumes the return eliminates all applicable ordering and transaction records.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A return to the supplier is exempt from all Schedule II transaction documentation.
Expiration removes the controlled status and all inventory responsibility immediately.
Any patient return can be processed as a registrant-to-supplier stock purchase reversal.
The applicable Form 222 or CSOS ordering pathway is distinct from the Form 106 loss report.

visible.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy discovers a reportable theft and plans to withhold the initial written DEA notice until a final quantity investigation is complete.

Case B: Staff confuse the current provision's completed electronic Form 106 period with the separate initial-notice deadline.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A confirmed theft needs no report whenever only a small quantity was taken.
Only losses above a universal fixed dollar threshold can be significant under the described rule.
The applicable initial written DEA notice is due within one business day of discovery.
The completed Form 106 clock is a new 45 days beginning only after the pharmacy finishes its investigation.

visible.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy removes controlled stock from its computer and peels off its labels, then records the medication as physically destroyed.

Case B: A registered reverse distributor receives controlled drugs for destruction and confuses its receipt-based 30-day rule with a general pharmacy deadline after expiration.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Deleting an inventory entry or label does not make the substance non-retrievable.
Applicable destruction records and witness conditions are distinct from a universal requirement for two pharmacists.
Every partly used inventory bottle qualifies as immediate-administration residue exempt from the described Form 41 record.
The described reverse-distributor clock starts at receipt for destruction, not every pharmacy product's expiration.

visible.stem:
Case A: A newly registered location begins controlled-substance activity with no controlled stock and proposes skipping its initial inventory.

Case B: A previously unscheduled substance becomes controlled on a specified effective date, and staff schedule its first inventory for the next routine biennial count.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A zero-stock initial inventory is still recorded for the new activity.
A head office's aggregate estimate always replaces inventories at separately registered locations.
The newly scheduled substance has an effective-date inventory requirement rather than waiting for the next routine count.
The biennial interval cannot exceed the applicable two-year maximum.

visible.stem:
Case A: For the federal inventory rule described, an opened Schedule III container holds exactly 1,000 tablets, and another holds 1,001 tablets.

Case B: An opened Schedule II container holds fewer tablets, and staff propose estimating its contents because the quantity is below 1,000.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The date alone makes opening-versus-closing information unnecessary.
An opened Schedule II container below 1,000 may be estimated under the III-V rule.
The over-1000 exact-count trigger distinguishes 1,001 from exactly 1,000 for the described III-V rule.
One total for all strengths and forms of the same ingredient satisfies every inventory-detail requirement.

visible.stem:
Case A: A medicine's current labeling requires a condition outside the pharmacy's general refrigerator or freezer ranges, but staff use the general range without checking the product.

Case B: A pharmacy stores medication in a dorm-style refrigerator with a small freezer compartment inside the refrigerator and also keeps staff meals there.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The actual product's approved storage and stability requirements must be considered rather than replaced by a general range.
Unopened manufacturer expiration applies unchanged after every reconstitution or opening.
A closed refrigerator door alone proves suitable medication storage.
A dorm-style unit containing staff meals is compliant whenever it feels cold.

visible.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy checks and records its medication temperature only once per day, though the described Board policy calls for two reviews and records daily.

Case B: After an excursion, the unit returns to normal temperature and staff release quarantined products without evaluating exposure duration or stability evidence.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Return to normal temperature does not erase the previous excursion's possible effect.
A closed pharmacy has no need to detect out-of-range storage on those days.
The described temperature and excursion records have a minimum one-year retention requirement.
The one-check schedule does not meet the described twice-daily review-and-record structure.

visible.stem:
Case A: A delivery invoice is present, but the incoming package has damaged seals and an unresolved temperature history.

Case B: The pharmacy plans to mail a lawful prescription using packaging that will freeze a temperature-sensitive medicine against a cold pack.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A lawful dispensing automatically makes every chosen mailing method permissible.
A valid prescription makes medication-stability protection during shipping unnecessary.
An invoice does not establish that a damaged or temperature-exposed product is usable.
Using a common carrier transfers every quality obligation away from the pharmacy.

visible.stem:
Case A: A technician performs permitted remote information processing and assumes that this authorizes offsite final product verification and independent dispensing.

Case B: A Massachusetts final-dispensing location is staffed without an onsite pharmacist, relying solely on a telepharmacy arrangement modeled on another state.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Remote processing does not itself grant final product-verification or dispensing authority.
Every Schedule VI drug qualifies for the same central-fill direct-to-patient exception.
Another state's technician-only model establishes the Massachusetts onsite-staffing rule.
Every compounded preparation may be supplied through central fill merely because both pharmacies are licensed.

visible.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy calls its patient-facing pickup device a locker and stocks Schedule II medicine and a product requiring refrigeration.

Case B: The locker releases eligible medicines after usual pharmacy hours without offering pharmacist consultation during those operating hours.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The pharmacy may require every patient to use the APS with no choice.
Usual daytime pharmacy hours are the only consultation hours required even while the APS dispenses at night.
A working access code replaces all location, Board approval, and audit-trail conditions.
The device's name does not avoid the APS restrictions, including the stated Schedule IV-VI scope and excluded storage types.

visible.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy's processing machine mixes several lots in one cell, and one of those lots is recalled.

Case B: A healthcare-facility automated dispensing device releases medication without a valid patient-specific prescription or order because the device was previously approved.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Every automated device has one identical patient-release authority.
An approved facility device independently authorizes dispensing without patient orders.
The pharmacy must be able to quarantine the commingled lots appropriately when a lot is recalled.
Barcode-enabled automation eliminates all pharmacist final-validation responsibility.

visible.stem:
Case A: A supplier provides a certificate of analysis for a bulk ingredient, but the pharmacy has not established that the ingredient is eligible for its proposed section 503A use.

Case B: A different container is labeled research use only, yet an employee proposes using it for a patient's injectable preparation because the powder appears identical to a pharmaceutical ingredient.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A certificate of analysis does not by itself establish the ingredient's legal eligibility for the proposed compounding use.
The applicable bulk-substance pathway, manufacturer registration, and valid analytical documentation must be assessed together.
Keeping a supplier's general catalog makes batch-specific ingredient traceability unnecessary.
The research-use-only material is not justified for the proposed human injectable merely by its appearance.

visible.stem:
Case A: A prescriber documents that a patient cannot use a dye in a commercial product and specifies a clinically meaningful individualized alternative.

Case B: An unrelated pharmacy wants to copy a marketed product solely because its own shelf is empty and its proposed copy would cost less; it has not established a current FDA shortage or another applicable exception.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The second pharmacy has not established a permitted copying pathway merely through local stock shortage and price.
Technical ability to prepare the formula establishes that copying restrictions are satisfied.
A shortage-related exception or enforcement policy must be evaluated for the actual product, pathway, and relevant time.
The documented patient-specific difference is relevant to evaluating the permitted compounding pathway.

visible.stem:
Case A: A drug-store pharmacy without the applicable complex nonsterile authority plans a preparation classified as complex under the Massachusetts policy.

Case B: The pharmacy proposes crushing hazardous tablets into a suspension using an assessment of risk previously written only for counting intact tablets.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Obtaining the complex license eliminates the separate need to assess hazardous-drug controls.
The intact-tablet assessment does not establish adequate controls for the proposed crushing and compounding activity.
A change in USP terminology does not itself repeal Massachusetts facility-licensing categories.
The pharmacy must establish the additional authority required for its actual complex nonsterile activity.

visible.stem:
Case A: A patient's agent requests flavoring of an eligible Schedule VI medication under the described Massachusetts policy pathway.

Case B: A technician proposes using a different diluent and concentration from a kit's manufacturer-approved directions, while continuing to classify the process as unchanged manufacturer-directed reconstitution.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The Schedule VI flavoring permission also authorizes any formulation change to Schedule II–V medicines.
The eligible flavoring pathway still requires evaluation and documentation of stability, compatibility, and therapeutic intent.
The preparation remains within the unchanged-instructions exception whenever the original kit is used.
Calling an activity tablet splitting settles its classification without reviewing the product.

visible.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy keeps an approved recipe with ingredients, amounts, instructions, packaging, and the basis for its assigned beyond-use date.

Case B: After preparing a batch, the pharmacy has no record of the actual ingredient lots, preparation time, personnel, yield, or checks because staff believe the stored recipe is sufficient.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The approved recipe serves a master-formulation function rather than documenting every actual batch.
A master formula removes the need for a record of actual quantities, personnel, and quality checks.
The batch's identification can be disconnected from ingredient and quality records once the label is printed.
A short preparation time makes any omitted compounding record eligible for simplified treatment.

visible.stem:
Case A: A nonpreserved aqueous compounded preparation has water activity at or above 0.6, and no applicable preparation-specific monograph or supporting stability data establishes a different limit.

Case B: A second preparation is a nonaqueous oral liquid with water activity below 0.6 under the same no-specific-data assumption; a component or product condition may impose a shorter limit.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The second preparation receives 180 days merely because it is nonaqueous.
The preserved aqueous default is 35 days only when frozen.
A default maximum permits ignoring a shorter demonstrated stability limitation.
The stated default for the first preparation is a maximum 14 days under refrigeration, subject to shorter applicable limits.

visible.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy has an ISO 5 primary engineering control in an unclassified segregated compounding area and proposes assigning Category 2 conditions based only on the hood classification.

Case B: A second pharmacy describes Category 3 as a drug-toxicity classification and assumes it has no relation to facilities, testing, or allowed beyond-use dates.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A product-protective positive-pressure workbench necessarily provides hazardous-drug containment.
Category 3 is a compounding framework involving additional conditions, not a toxicity grade for the ingredient.
An ISO 5 hood in the described SCA does not by itself establish the cleanroom conditions for Category 2 preparation.
Facility category, personnel qualification, monitoring, testing, and BUD restrictions must be considered together.

visible.stem:
Case A: Preparation of an otherwise eligible immediate-use CSP starts at 8:00 AM and finishes at 8:25 AM. Administration is planned to begin at 12:15 PM.

Case B: A separate otherwise eligible preparation combines four different sterile products, but a staff member argues that small quantities make it fit the described three-product immediate-use limit.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Four different sterile products satisfy the stated limit when each amount is small.
The proposed 12:15 PM start exceeds four hours from the 8:00 AM preparation start.
Immediate-use status authorizes retaining and sharing leftover single-dose contents among patients.
The entire infusion must finish within four hours for the described start-of-administration condition to be met.

visible.stem:
Case A: A Massachusetts preparation is subject to a sterility-testing requirement, but the pharmacy wants to dispense it while the result is pending and recall it later if the result fails.

Case B: Another preparation passed a sterility test, and the pharmacist is asked to conclude that this also proves acceptable potency and absence of endotoxin.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The described Massachusetts policy requires a negative sterility result before dispensing a CSP for which that testing is required.
A negative sterility result replaces the remaining pre-release visual and documentation checks.
Using a 0.2-micrometer filter establishes endotoxin removal and a longer BUD without additional evidence.
Passing a sterility test establishes acceptable potency and endotoxin status for the same batch.

visible.stem:
Case A: A medication is not federally scheduled, but its handling can expose workers to a hazardous drug. Staff propose excluding it from the pharmacy's hazardous-drug assessment solely because it has no DEA schedule.

Case B: A compounding activity uses a hazardous active pharmaceutical ingredient; the manager proposes using a routine assessment of risk to waive the required containment.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: An ingredient's generic name is sufficient to assess risk without its dosage form or manipulation.
A medication can be subject to either hazardous-drug controls or DEA controls, but not both.
A routine assessment of risk can waive containment for any hazardous active pharmaceutical ingredient.
Lack of a DEA schedule does not establish that a medicine is nonhazardous for occupational handling.

visible.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy selects gloves based only on their nitrile material and has not established the applicable chemotherapy-glove performance or suitability for sterile hazardous preparation.

Case B: A new employee will independently handle hazardous drugs before role-specific training because the next annual competency assessment is scheduled soon.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The HD designated-person title has the identical qualification rule as every nonsterile designated-pharmacist role.
Containment must be selected for the sterile or nonsterile activity and its exposure pathway.
A future annual competency date does not replace training needed before independent hazardous-drug duties.
Glove material alone does not establish the required chemotherapy-tested performance and task suitability.

visible.stem:
Case A: After a hazardous-drug manipulation, an employee uses an alcohol wipe and documents that deactivation, decontamination, cleaning, and disinfection are all established by that one action.

Case B: A returned material is both hazardous and federally controlled, but staff select a disposal vendor solely because it accepts ordinary pharmaceutical returns.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Agent selection, contact time, sequence, compatibility, and personnel protection belong in the applicable procedure.
The single wipe does not establish that all four distinct hazardous-residue and microbial-control objectives were met.
The disposal pathway must be assessed for both hazardous-waste and controlled-substance requirements that apply.
A visibly damaged hazardous-drug package should be opened at the normal receiving counter to identify the leak.

visible.stem:
Case A: An outsourcing facility relies on section 503B to supply eligible office-use stock and argues that it has the same cGMP exemption as qualifying section 503A preparations.

Case B: The facility tells purchasers that appearing in FDA's outsourcing-facility registration system means every compounded medicine it makes has individual FDA approval.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Outsourcing-facility registration does not constitute individual FDA approval of every compounded product.
Federal permission to supply eligible office-use stock does not remove the need for a valid prescription when dispensing prescription drugs to an individual patient.
Federal outsourcing registration by itself establishes the required Massachusetts facility authority.
The described section 503B pathway remains subject to cGMP requirements.

visible.stem:
Case A: A section 503B facility proposes using a bulk substance merely because it has a certificate of analysis, without establishing a qualifying clinical-need or shortage pathway.

Case B: A third party proposes buying compounded drugs from the outsourcing facility for ordinary wholesale resale, rather than dispensing under patient prescriptions or administering in a healthcare setting.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The certificate does not replace the bulk-substance eligibility conditions for section 503B.
A shortage at any historical time is sufficient for all later compounding, distribution, and dispensing.
The ordinary wholesale-resale plan is not justified by the described patient-dispensing or healthcare-administration pathways.
Essentially-copy and unsafe-or-ineffective withdrawal restrictions remain relevant to eligibility.

visible.stem:
Case A: An outsourcing facility submits its annual registration in the October 1 through December 31 window and assumes that no separate drug-product report is required.

Case B: The facility supplies a preparation without a patient-specific prescription, but its label omits the applicable Office Use Only and Not for Resale statements.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Product reports are limited to products that already have individual FDA marketing approval.
A facility registration number substitutes for the described office-use and resale statements.
Annual registration and the separate initial and June/December product-reporting obligations are distinct.
A compounded-drug statement makes lot and storage information unnecessary.

visible.stem:
Case A: A sponsor has an investigational new drug pathway for clinical research and describes it to a retail pharmacy as approval to market the product for routine patient prescriptions.

Case B: A different product has an approved ANDA, and staff assume this permits substituting it for products with other routes and release formulations without a product-specific interchange assessment.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: An IND-related research pathway is not the same as marketing approval for routine retail sale.
A BLA is the individual dispensing pharmacist's professional license.
ANDA approval establishes pharmacist substitution across all routes and release formulations of the ingredient.
Submitting an NDA establishes that the proposed drug is approved for marketing.

visible.stem:
Case A: A wholesaler presents an NDC number and a searchable label listing as proof that a particular product has FDA marketing approval.

Case B: A pharmacist sees an emergency-use authorization and treats it as unrestricted full approval without checking the authorization's current conditions or covered population.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: An EUA removes the need to check the authorized population and conditions of use.
An approved product's off-label use creates general independent prescribing authority for pharmacists.
Every OTC medicine is marketed through the monograph pathway and none through an approved application.
The identifier and listing do not by themselves establish FDA approval of the specific product.

visible.stem:
Case A: A dispenser qualifies for a documented exemption covering specified enhanced DSCSA requirements during a defined period.

Case B: The dispenser therefore proposes purchasing from unqualified suppliers and dispensing suspect products without investigation, although those obligations are not among the exempted requirements.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Submitting an exemption request has the same effect as receiving a currently effective exemption.
The specified enhanced-requirement exemption also waives the unrelated supplier and suspect-product duties.
The dispenser must identify precisely which requirements and time period the exemption covers.
Describing the pharmacy as small establishes eligibility without applying the actual criteria.

visible.stem:
Case A: A pharmacist identifies credible signs that a received product may be illegitimate but has not completed the required investigation.

Case B: After investigation, the product is determined to be illegitimate. Staff propose waiting until a routine monthly report to notify the appropriate parties.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The suspect-product situation calls for segregation and investigation rather than routine dispensing while uncertainty remains.
FDA Form 3911 is the DEA form used instead of Form 106 for controlled-drug theft.
A quarantine can be ended solely to free storage space while the investigation remains unresolved.
A monthly report satisfies the stated 24-hour notification requirement after illegitimate-product determination.

visible.stem:
Case A: A manufacturer removes a marketed product for a violation that would support FDA legal action and describes the action as a routine commercial withdrawal.

Case B: Another manufacturer retrieves a lot still entirely under its direct control; none of that lot has been released for sale or use.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A recall-related correction requires physical transport of every affected product.
The second situation is necessarily a patient-level recall even though none of the lot was released.
Classifying an action as non-recall eliminates any other patient-safety or reporting obligation.
The first action fits the described recall concept rather than becoming a market withdrawal merely through the firm's chosen label.

visible.stem:
Case A: A company begins a recall and notifies the pharmacy before FDA assigns a risk classification. Staff plan to continue dispensing the affected lot until a class appears.

Case B: A separate recalled product is classified as Class III, and a technician assumes the pharmacy can disregard the recall because serious harm is unlikely.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Class III makes compliance with the recall instructions optional.
Class I means a low probability of any health consequence and is the least serious category.
Lack of a completed FDA classification does not justify continuing to dispense the affected lot contrary to the recall instructions.
The recall class alone identifies which patients received the affected lot.

visible.stem:
Case A: A pharmacist catches an incorrect strength before it reaches the patient. The system records it as a near miss.

Case B: A properly dispensed commercial medicine causes an adverse reaction, while a different preparation has a quality defect but has not yet harmed a patient.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The first situation is not the same as the policy's patient-received QRE definition, although it remains relevant to safety improvement.
Correct product selection and labeling rule out any subsequent adverse reaction.
A preparation cannot be considered defective unless patient injury has already occurred.
An adverse event and a product defect are the same category with the same trigger in every case.

visible.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy maintains only a list of employees associated with errors, with no documented analysis of contributing factors or prevention process.

Case B: After adopting a workflow change, the pharmacy never checks whether staff follow it or whether the targeted problem recurs.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The program should focus only on assigning blame because system factors are outside CQI.
Adopting a workflow change establishes effectiveness without further evaluation.
CQI education is needed only when the pharmacy first opens.
Identifying an employee alone does not provide the described written CQI program's detection, assessment, and prevention functions.

visible.stem:
Case A: A pharmacist learns of a QRE at 10:00 AM Monday but proposes waiting until Friday's completed investigation to begin the initial record.

Case B: The pharmacy has notified the patient and given corrective instructions, yet staff assume that this makes a written CQI record unnecessary.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: An initial record must be delayed until every contributing factor is conclusively known.
Initial documentation is due within the described 24 hours after discovery or notification, not after the investigation ends.
The described QRE records are retained for at least two years from the QRE report date.
Patient communication does not replace the required CQI documentation.

visible.stem:
Case A: A resident pharmacy's MOR discovers both improper dispensing and the resulting serious injury on the same day. No uncertainty about which fact was discovered first exists in this case.

Case B: After filing the applicable Board report, staff propose retaining the associated records for only the general two-year prescription-record period.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The event requires the applicable prompt Board reporting with the described seven-business-day outside limit.
The Board report does not replace patient notification and applicable CQI duties.
Nonresident status makes improper dispensing into Massachusetts exempt from Board reporting.
The described improper-dispensing report records require at least five years from Board-report filing.

visible.stem:
Case A: An employee learns that a drug produced by the pharmacy is associated with an event satisfying the applicable Massachusetts SADE trigger. The MOR first reads the employee's message three days later.

Case B: The preparation is also suspected to be defective and to have caused the SADE, bringing the described immediate defective-preparation policy into the assessment.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The described state pathway connects reporting to the Board, FDA MedWatch, and the Betsy Lehman Center.
Every ordinary side effect of any commercial medicine meets this pharmacy-produced SADE trigger.
The employee-awareness trigger is not postponed until the MOR opens the message.
The immediate defective-preparation policy cannot be ignored merely because a general seven-business-day provision exists.

visible.stem:
Case A: A section 503B outsourcing facility receives initial information about a serious and unexpected adverse drug experience involving its compounded prescription drug.

Case B: Material follow-up information arrives later, but the facility plans to hold it until the next annual registration renewal.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Follow-up information is reported only during annual registration.
The described adverse-experience records have no retention requirement after report submission.
The described initial FDA report is due as soon as possible and no later than 15 calendar days after initial receipt.
The federal 15-day limit removes any applicable faster Massachusetts reporting duty.

visible.stem:
Case A: An ISO 5 viable air result is 2 CFU per cubic meter per media device. Staff compare it with the described action level of greater than 1 CFU.

Case B: A separate ISO 5 surface result is exactly 3 CFU per media device, and staff compare it with the described surface threshold of greater than 3 CFU.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The first result exceeds the stated ISO 5 viable-air action threshold.
An action-level result can be dismissed solely because the preparation looks clear.
Exactly 3 CFU exceeds the stated greater-than-3 threshold because greater than means greater than or equal to.
Air and surface CFU results can use an identical denominator without regard to sampling method.

visible.stem:
Case A: A laboratory reports viable-air counts per cubic meter, but staff treat that unit as one liter when comparing it with the policy's air limits.

Case B: A pass-through connects two different ISO-classified spaces, and personnel apply the less clean space's threshold without considering the stated policy rule.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: One cubic meter corresponds to 1,000 liters, so the reported denominator must not be treated as one liter.
The same numeric CFU threshold applies to every ISO class and measurement type.
The described pass-through rule uses the cleaner connected space's ISO classification.
Results from distinct sites or media devices should not be combined into an invented cumulative comparison.
